abstract.t: A profile of RFC 5869 for nish/crypto/hkdf: HKDF instantiated with SHA-256, so HashLen is 32, and the forms of it that hold the keying material as a Secret, for SHA-256 and SHA-384. Every requirement quotes RFC 5869, the main source; every binding sentence of RFC 5869 (MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHALL NOT, REQUIRED) is tested or excluded here.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
nish/crypto/hkdf exports HKDF-Extract and HKDF-Expand for SHA-256. The properties compare them with nish/crypto/hmac, the HMAC-SHA-256 they are built on.

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: nish/crypto/hkdf export const hkdfExtractSha256 = (salt: u8[], ikm: u8[]): u8[] export const hkdfExpandSha256 = (prk: u8[], info: u8[], length: i32): u8[] | null export const hkdfExtractSha384 = (salt: u8[], ikm: u8[]): u8[] export const hkdfExpandSha384 = (prk: u8[], info: u8[], length: i32): u8[] | null export const hkdfExtractSha256Secret = (salt: u8[], ikm: Secret<u8[]>): Secret<u8[]> export const hkdfExtractSha384Secret = (salt: u8[], ikm: Secret<u8[]>): Secret<u8[]> export const hkdfExpandSha256Secret = (prk: Secret<u8[]>, info: u8[], length: i32): Secret<u8[]> | null export const hkdfExpandSha384Secret = (prk: Secret<u8[]>, info: u8[], length: i32): Secret<u8[]> | null export const hkdfSha256Secret = (salt: u8[], ikm: Secret<u8[]>, info: u8[], length: i32): Secret<u8[]> | null export const hkdfSha384Secret = (salt: u8[], ikm: Secret<u8[]>, info: u8[], length: i32): Secret<u8[]> | null // module: nish/crypto/hmac export const hmacSha256 = (key: u8[], data: u8[]): u8[] export const hmacSha384 = (key: u8[], data: u8[]): u8[]

section.name: Extract
section.sourcecode: // P-EXTRACT-IS-HMAC covers R-EXTRACT — HKDF-Extract is HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by the salt forall (salt: u8[] /* 1..150 */, ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha256(salt, ikm) === hmacSha256(salt, ikm)

blockquote.t: if not provided, it is set to a string of HashLen zeros.

section.sourcecode: // P-EMPTY-SALT covers R-SALT — an absent salt is HashLen zero octets forall (ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha256([], ikm) === hmacSha256(zeros(32), ikm)

blockquote.t: PRK a pseudorandom key (of HashLen octets)

section.sourcecode: // P-PRK-LEN covers R-PRK-LEN — the PRK is HashLen octets forall (salt: u8[] /* 0..150 */, ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha256(salt, ikm).length === 32

section.name: Expand

blockquote.t: L length of output keying material in octets (<= 255*HashLen)

section.t: Note: The RFC states the bound; refusing a longer L with null is how nish/crypto/hkdf honours it.

blockquote.t: info optional context and application specific information (can be a zero-length string)
OKM output keying material (of L octets)

section.sourcecode: // P-EXPAND-LENGTH covers R-L, R-OKM-LEN — Expand gives exactly L octets for L <= 255*HashLen and refuses a longer L forall (prk: u8[] /* 32..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..40 */, n: i32 /* 0..8300 */) => implies(n <= 255 * 32, hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, n) !== null && unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, n)).length === n) && implies(n > 255 * 32, hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, n) === null)

blockquote.t: OKM = first L octets of T
T(0) = empty string (zero length) T(1) = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T(0) | info | 0x01) T(2) = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T(1) | info | 0x02)

section.sourcecode: // P-T1-T2 covers R-T — the first two blocks are T(1) and T(2) as §2.3 defines them forall (prk: u8[] /* 32..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..100 */) => unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, 64)).slice(0, 32) === hmacSha256(prk, info.concat([01])) && unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, 64)).slice(32, 64) === hmacSha256(prk, hmacSha256(prk, info.concat([01])).concat(info).concat([02]))

section.name: Secret Forms
section.t: nish/crypto/hkdf also exports each derivation with its keying material held as a Secret<u8[]>, for SHA-256 and SHA-384. What a Secret form adds is wiping, which a functional test cannot observe and tests/wipes/crypto.js holds; the properties here hold each to the same output as its plain twin. RFC 5869 Appendix A has no SHA-384 test case, so SHA-384's plain forms are held to HMAC-SHA-384 by the definitions above, with HashLen 48, and its Secret forms to them.
section.sourcecode: // P-EXTRACT-IS-HMAC-384 covers R-EXTRACT — HKDF-Extract over SHA-384 is HMAC-SHA-384 keyed by the salt forall (salt: u8[] /* 1..150 */, ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha384(salt, ikm) === hmacSha384(salt, ikm)
// P-EMPTY-SALT-384 covers R-SALT — an absent salt is HashLen zero octets, 48 for SHA-384 forall (ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha384([], ikm) === hmacSha384(zeros(48), ikm)

// P-T1-T2-384 covers R-T — over SHA-384, the first two blocks are T(1) and T(2) as §2.3 defines them forall (prk: u8[] /* 48..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..100 */) => unwrap(hkdfExpandSha384(prk, info, 96)).slice(0, 48) === hmacSha384(prk, info.concat([01])) && unwrap(hkdfExpandSha384(prk, info, 96)).slice(48, 96) === hmacSha384(prk, hmacSha384(prk, info.concat([01])).concat(info).concat([02]))

// P-EXPAND-LENGTH-384 covers R-L, R-OKM-LEN — over SHA-384, Expand gives exactly L octets for L <= 255*HashLen and refuses a longer L forall (prk: u8[] /* 48..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..40 */, n: i32 /* 0..12400 */) => implies(n <= 255 * 48, hkdfExpandSha384(prk, info, n) !== null && unwrap(hkdfExpandSha384(prk, info, n)).length === n) && implies(n > 255 * 48, hkdfExpandSha384(prk, info, n) === null)

// P-SECRET-EXTRACT covers R-EXTRACT — hkdfExtractSha256Secret and hkdfExtractSha384Secret, given the IKM as a Secret, give the PRK their plain twins give forall (salt: u8[] /* 0..150 */, ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha256Secret(salt, ikm) === hkdfExtractSha256(salt, ikm) && hkdfExtractSha384Secret(salt, ikm) === hkdfExtractSha384(salt, ikm)

// P-SECRET-EXPAND-256 covers R-L, R-OKM-FIRST — hkdfExpandSha256Secret, given the PRK as a Secret, gives the OKM hkdfExpandSha256 gives and refuses the L it refuses forall (prk: u8[] /* 32..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..40 */, n: i32 /* 0..8300 */) => implies(n <= 255 * 32, unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256Secret(prk, info, n)) === unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, n))) && implies(n > 255 * 32, hkdfExpandSha256Secret(prk, info, n) === null)

// P-SECRET-EXPAND-384 covers R-L, R-OKM-FIRST — hkdfExpandSha384Secret, given the PRK as a Secret, gives the OKM hkdfExpandSha384 gives and refuses the L it refuses forall (prk: u8[] /* 48..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..40 */, n: i32 /* 0..12400 */) => implies(n <= 255 * 48, unwrap(hkdfExpandSha384Secret(prk, info, n)) === unwrap(hkdfExpandSha384(prk, info, n))) && implies(n > 255 * 48, hkdfExpandSha384Secret(prk, info, n) === null)

// P-SECRET-HKDF covers R-EXTRACT, R-OKM-FIRST — hkdfSha256Secret and hkdfSha384Secret are Expand of Extract, as their plain twins compose forall (salt: u8[] /* 0..64 */, ikm: u8[] /* 0..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..40 */, n: i32 /* 0..300 */) => unwrap(hkdfSha256Secret(salt, ikm, info, n)) === unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(hkdfExtractSha256(salt, ikm), info, n)) && unwrap(hkdfSha384Secret(salt, ikm, info, n)) === unwrap(hkdfExpandSha384(hkdfExtractSha384(salt, ikm), info, n))

section.name: Out of Scope
section.t: This contract tests hkdfExtractSha256 and hkdfExpandSha256, their SHA-384 twins and the six Secret forms above; every other export of nish/crypto/hkdf is declared out of scope below, with the reason it is not tested.
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha256, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha384, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha256Secret, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha384Secret, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869

Out of scope: hkdfExtractInto, an allocation-free variant writing into caller buffers through an HkdfScratch; its (out, at) is an /* out hashLength */ write, but its first parameter is the class HkdfScratch, which vector 0.6.0 refuses in a ts-interface block ("HkdfScratch is not a ts-interface type; use u8[], string, boolean, i8, i16, i32, i64, u8, u16, u32, u64, f64, Secret<u8[]>, u16[], u32[], u64[], each optionally | null"), and it returns void where an /* out CAP */ write returns the end offset

Out of scope: hkdfExpandInto, an allocation-free variant writing into caller buffers through an HkdfScratch; its first parameter is the class HkdfScratch, which vector 0.6.0 refuses in a ts-interface block ("HkdfScratch is not a ts-interface type; use u8[], string, boolean, i8, i16, i32, i64, u8, u16, u32, u64, f64, Secret<u8[]>, u16[], u32[], u64[], each optionally | null"), and its (out, at) is followed by the length and answers a boolean where an /* out CAP */ write returns the end offset

Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelInto, an allocation-free variant writing into caller buffers through an HkdfScratch; its context is a /* window */, but its first parameter is the class HkdfScratch, which vector 0.6.0 refuses in a ts-interface block ("HkdfScratch is not a ts-interface type; use u8[], string, boolean, i8, i16, i32, i64, u8, u16, u32, u64, f64, Secret<u8[]>, u16[], u32[], u64[], each optionally | null"), it returns void where an /* out CAP */ write returns the end offset, and it is RFC 8446's Expand-Label, not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha256Held, Expand-Label of a held Secret PRK, written in place into a Secret or a caller buffer; likewise RFC 8446, not RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha384Held, Expand-Label of a held Secret PRK, written in place into a Secret or a caller buffer; likewise RFC 8446, not RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelHeldInto, Expand-Label of a held Secret PRK, written in place into a Secret or a caller buffer; likewise RFC 8446, not RFC 5869
Out of scope: HkdfScratch, a class holding reusable buffers, not a function; the profile declares functions only

RFC 5869 A.1: HKDF-Expand gives the printed OKM (L = 42)

abstract.t: This document specifies a simple Hashed Message Authentication Code (HMAC)-based key derivation function (HKDF), which can be used as a building block in various protocols and applications. The key derivation function (KDF) is intended to support a wide range of applications and requirements, and is conservative in its use of cryptographic hash functions. This document is not an Internet Standards Track specification; it is published for informational purposes.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
